open_points.subject: shared Port declaration validation
open_points.text: `models` “Must not own: Validation”; `functions` owns “A02”; while `bindings` must reject ports that “break a rule A02 sets for contract ports” and modules on one line “do not know each other.”
open_points.question: Which lower module owns the reusable validation of Port declarations—including schema-subset validity, unique names, carriage/media-type rules and disclosure-class placement—so both `functions` and `bindings` can apply the same rules without duplicating ownership or creating a forbidden dependency?
options: `functions` owns it and `bindings` is allowed to depend on `functions`
`functions` and `bindings` each own separate copies of the rules
A new lower-level validation module owns it
open_points.default_guess: Make `canonical_values` own and expose the shared Port-declaration validator, leaving contextual refusal ordering to each caller.

open_points.subject: randomly minted entity identifiers
open_points.text: “Every record is written through `store`, which owns its persistence”; “Most record types have one writing module”; A01 says `trial_execution_id`, `binding_id`, `run_id`, `approval_id` and `grant_id` are “minted at random by the kernel” and collisions are minted again.
open_points.question: Which module owns random identifier generation and collision handling for each entity: `store`, each record-owning module, or a shared lower-level capability?
options: `store` mints and collision-checks every random identifier atomically
Each record-owning module mints identifiers and retries after a store collision
A shared lower-level identifier generator mints them while `store` enforces uniqueness
open_points.default_guess: Let `store` mint and collision-check the identifiers inside the transaction that creates each record.

open_points.subject: Run outputs and status persistence
open_points.text: M19 defines `outputs`: “StoredValues by flow output port, as produced” and a stored `status`; State 3 says “The run's answer — status, outputs, and per flow output its value or the reason ... — is computed by `runs` from the trace when asked and is not stored,” but later says “the run's status and WaitingPoints M20 are derived from them and written by `runs`.”
open_points.question: Which Run facts are durable fields and which are derived on read: status, waiting points, produced output references, and final per-output reasons?
options: Persist status, waiting points and produced outputs as M19 states; derive only final reasons
Persist status and waiting points, but derive outputs and reasons from the graph, run inputs and trace
Persist none of the answer and derive status, outputs, waiting points and reasons entirely from records
open_points.default_guess: Persist status and waiting points as operational state, and derive produced outputs and final reasons through `runs.read_run`.
